newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end firm, Rhone busy.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end firm, Rhone busy.

text.p: The Paris bourse finished in positive ground for the third straight session this week since the Socialists came to power.
Traders said the market was enjoying a honeymoon period with the left and bargain hunting helped support prices.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 10.88 points or 0.41 percent at 2,635.37. The CAC-40 futures contract was up 10 at 2,614 from Tuesday's close.
Volume was a heavy 10.01 billion francs.
* Rhone jumped 5.38 percent to 199.8, on news a Merieux anti-aids drug is going to phase two trials in the U.S.
* Carrefour sheds 0.77 percent to 3,880, with investors taking profits after strong gains since Sunday.
* Other retailers hit by profit-taking were Pinault-Printemps, down 2.02 percent at 2,420 and Promodes, down 2.52 percent at 2,015.
* Thomson-CSF continues weak, undermined by expectations its privatisation will be dropped. Dassault Aviation rebounds, up 0.94 percent at 1,070.
* Lagardere also rallies, adds 2.11 percent to 169.5. But rival Thomson-CSF bidder, Alcatel Alsthom falls 1.75 percent to 619, after earlier recent gains.

* Renault adds 3.25 percent to 133.4 francs. The Socialist party said it wants the carmaker to suspend its closure of the Belgian Vilvoorde factory. The stock had been badly hit last week on fears that a Socialist win would block restructuring moves.
* Air Liquide gained 1.87 percent to 927. Two blocks of 373,000 shares traded, or one percent of the capital, at 912 and 913 francs per share.
* Bic rises 2.37 percent to 907 as investors pick consumer stocks.
* Sanofi ends 3.34 percent higher at 516. The group told shareholders 1997 profit growth would be in line with 1996, when it rose 11 percent.
* A firm dollar against the franc, at levels around 5.85 and last seen more than three years, also helped support share prices.
* Prime Minister Lionel Jospin is due to meet President Jacques Chirac at 1700 GMT on the composition of the new government. A first meeting in the afternoon went very well, Jospin said.
